newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Key Brazil area's soy crop to fall to 5.2 mln tns.
newsitem.headline: Key Brazil area's soy crop to fall to 5.2 mln tns.

text.p: The soybean crop in the key Brazilian growing state of Rio Grande do Sul could drop to 5.25 million tonnes from a previous forecast of 5.68 million tonnes, a division of the state's agricultural secretariat said.

"We have very localised information indicating there is damage to the crop due to dryness. That would cause a drop in productivity to 1,800 kilos per hectare which is a preliminary estimate," said Carlos Cardoso, economist at Emater.

Emater, which provides technical assistance to growers, previously calculated the soybean crop would be 5.68 million tonnes, based on planted area of 2,918,245 hectares and productivity of 1,947 kilos per hectare.
Cardoso emphasised the agency had still not calculated the total impact of recent dry weather in Rio Grande do Sul state would only confirm a final estimate next week.
"The reduction (in productivity) is not going to be less than five percent," he said.
